Two standalone verifiers reproduce 108 exactly rational reduced cases and 30 independent full-Liouvillian cases; finite tests are not substituted for the general proof.

value.rationale: A single localized excitation on a symmetric hub-and-spoke network is a natural transport problem, and full capture arises solely through environmental dephasing. The exact two-rate joint optimum scales as sqrt(m) with a sharp coefficient; the dark-state singularity explains divergent weak-noise capture time, the Zeno limit explains strong-noise cost, and the hub-started lifetime has a distinct noncommuting dephasing limit. These distinguish physically meaningful preparation and control protocols across an unbounded graph family. The result is not an arbitrary finite slice, only a textbook two-site special case, or a numerical optimization claim; no thermodynamic or experimental universality is asserted.
